text:
maya: heads-up — ACME Prod reporting a sudden uptick in 429s and long-tail latency on their Dedicated pool since ~08:30 UTC. Customer says autoscale isn't bringing nodes up fast enough. Repro steps below.

ops-bot: [alert] dedicated-autoscale-failure detected for cluster rdx-dedicated-eu-west-1 (A-8271) :rotating_light:

kevin: thx, can you grab the HPA/CA events + kube events and any recent CA logs?

arjun: pasted kube events from the failing deployment: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Normal   ScalingReplicaSet 3m    deployment/controller Scaled up replica set "acme-prod-xyz" to 1
  Warning  FailedCreate       3m    replicaset          Error creating: pods \"acme-prod-xyz-...\" is forbidden: quota exceeded: gpu-quota
```

arjun: also CA log snippet: `scale up inhibited: cloud quota 0/8 GPUs available in zone eu-west-1b`

maya: quick repro I used (minimal):
1) run 200 concurrent POSTs to /v1/generate for acme route
2) observe proxy queue climb and 429s

Example load loop: `for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY\" -d '{"input":"hi"}' & done`

maya: initial metrics: proxy.queue_length=147, proxy.reject_count=83, avg_inflight=12

kevin: hunch: we should be falling back to reserved-burst/backfill pools but something is blocking backfill. Can you check billing/reserved-pool flags?

nicholas: checked infra flags — a recent config flip prevented backfill for Dedicated profiles while we run a billing-migration test. That prevents cluster-autoscaler from triggering cross-pool backfill and effectively leaves CA waiting on zone quota. In short: CA sees 0 GPUs available and won't spin other pools.

maya: API proxy logs show repeated 429s and backlog while pods stay Pending: `pods pending: 6, pending_reason: Insufficient GPU`

kevin: immediate mitigation options: (A) increase minReplicas on the Deployment/Route so existing warm pods remain available for short bursts, (B) enable reserved-burst/backfill override for this account, (C) ask infra to temporarily lift the billing-block flag. I'll try (A) and (B).

kevin: running: `redwoodctl route update acme/prod --min-replicas 3` and `redwoodctl dedicated update --customer acme --reserved-burst=true`

ops-bot: runbook action: minReplicas increased 1->3 for route acme/prod (actioned by kevin)

sre-oncall: new nodes started provisioning at 08:48:05 UTC. Note: model containers still need ~60-90s to pull weights and init, so p95/p99 will remain high until warm caches populate. Recommend enabling prefix/KV cache and short pre-warm for heavy routes.

maya: told customer about the mitigations and ETA ~5-7m. They're ok with temporary minReplica bump. Will follow up on telemetry.

nicholas: filed INFRA-8921 to restore prioritized backfill for Dedicated and to add an alert when backfill is blocked by billing flags. Also adding CA policy test to catch this during canary flips.

maya: closing loop w/ customer once p99 < 500ms for 10m. Will update thread.

kevin: :thumbsup:
